seo.description: How your colour consultant works, how we work out how much paint you need, delivery in 3 days, payment and your photo.

faqs.question: How does the colour consultant choose my colours?
faqs.answer: It uses AI to look at your photo (the light, floors, furniture and colours already in the room) and read your brief. Then it picks three colours from our catalogue of real brand colours, and a suitable paint for each. It never makes up a colour.

faqs.question: How do you work out how much paint I need?
faqs.answer: We work out your wall area from the room size: the length and width of the room times the ceiling height, less a door and a window. We allow two coats plus 10% extra for cutting in and touch-ups, then choose the cheapest mix of tins that covers it.

faqs.question: Will the colour look the same on my wall?
faqs.answer: Screens show colours differently, and daylight changes them through the day. Use the swatch as a guide and paint a test patch before you do the whole room. Most colours have a sample pot you can order with your paint or on its own.

faqs.question: Can I order a sample first?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most colours. Each colour page shows the sample pot we can send in that colour: Plascon and Duram testers from R36 to R89, and Dulux’s R99 tester for the colours on its in-store colour wall. Prominent Paints doesn’t make sample pots, so its colour pages offer the smallest tin, 1 litre, instead. Samples are delivered in 3 days, like paint.

faqs.question: How fast is delivery?
faqs.answer: Your paint is delivered in 3 days.

faqs.question: How do I pay?
faqs.answer: Securely online through PayFast, by card or Instant EFT. We never see your card or banking details.

faqs.question: What happens to my photo?
faqs.answer: We send it to OpenAI only to get your colour suggestions and to paint the previews of your room, and we don’t keep it. OpenAI doesn’t use it to train its models.

samples.testTitle: How to test a sample pot
testSteps: Stir the pot well before you start.
Paint a patch at least the size of an A4 page, or paint a sheet of white card so you can move it around the room.
Give it two coats, and let the first coat dry before the second, as the instructions on the pot say.
Leave a hand’s width of plain wall between patches, so the colours don’t change how each other look.
Let it dry completely before you judge it. Paint often looks lighter or darker when it’s wet.
Look at it in the morning, at midday and in the evening, and with your lights on at night.
Try it on more than one wall. The wall with the window in it gets less direct light and looks darker than the wall opposite.
Hold your floor, curtains, cushions or a piece of furniture next to it to see how they go together.
samples.nextBody: Go back to your colour, or start a consultation with your room size, and we’ll work out exactly how much paint you need and what it costs. A few days after your samples arrive, we’ll email you once to see how the test patches look.
